question.text: Harish, an RTA executive, receives a call from a major institutional shareholder wanting to submit a representation letter for the AGM scheduled for Monday at 11:00 AM. It is now Saturday at 10:00 AM. Can the representation letter still be accepted, applying the "at least 48 hours before the AGM" rule?

answer.text: Yes, because the letter is being submitted more than 48 hours before the AGM
No, because representation letters must be submitted at least 7 days before the AGM
No, because no documents can be accepted over the weekend
Yes, but only if the shareholder holds more than 10% of the company's shares

explanation.text: The Logic: Proxy forms and financial institution representation letters must be received by the company at least 48 hours before the time fixed for the AGM. The AGM is on Monday at 11:00 AM and the letter is submitted on Saturday at 10:00 AM - a gap of 49 hours, which exceeds the 48-hour minimum. The submission is valid (option A). It is a calendar-time requirement, not a business-hours requirement. The Trap: Option B invokes a 7-day rule that does not apply. Option C invents a weekend ban. Option D adds an irrelevant 10% threshold. In the original ambiguous version the stem only said "Monday morning", so Saturday 10:00 AM could be less than, equal to, or more than 48 hours before the AGM - making option A defensible only under a particular meeting-time assumption. Note: The original question was ambiguous because it did not state the exact AGM time. The stem has been tightened to "Monday at 11:00 AM" so that the 49-hour gap is unambiguously more than 48 hours, making option A uniquely correct. Source: NISM Series II-A (RTA Corporate), Oct 2025, p.161.
